# §5 Commerce Analytics — Highlight Candidates

1. **8,295 eCat orders generated $8.0M in platform GMV over the trailing 12 months** — monthly volumes have been remarkably stable in the 600–784 range since mid-2025, with October 2025 peaking at $1.07M GMV and July 2025 at 784 orders. [→ §commerce]
2. **Quote orders carry a 3.3× AOV premium ($3,172 vs. $968 overall)** — with only 275 quotes representing 3.3% of volume but 10.9% of GMV trailing 12 months, quote adoption is an under-leveraged revenue lever. [→ §commerce]
3. **eCat Online now represents 47% of platform order volume** — buyer self-service is approaching parity with iPad (53%), and in April 2026 MTD online has pulled ahead at 55%. iPad still drives 65% of GMV due to its 1.6× AOV premium. [→ §commerce]
4. **Buyer base is exceptionally well diversified** — top 5 buyers account for only 10.7% of eCat GMV, with no single buyer exceeding 2.7%. The mix includes high-frequency retail accounts (Ivy Home: 348 orders) and low-frequency high-value designers (Saybrook Home: $10,473 AOV). [→ §commerce]
5. **HFC orders average $6,834 per order (7.1× overall AOV)** — the 93 HFC orders trailing 12 months generated $635,530 in GMV, signaling these hold-for-confirmation transactions involve complex or bulk commitments. [→ §commerce]
6. **All-channel business data reflects partial sync** — platform GMV ($8.0M) exceeds the synced all-channel total ($2.6M), preventing reliable share-of-business analysis until sync coverage expands. [→ §commerce]

## Priority Action Candidate
- **EXPAND QUOTE WORKFLOW ADOPTION**: 275 quotes generated $872K at 3.3× the average order value trailing 12 months. Encouraging more reps to use the quote workflow for complex or large-quantity transactions could meaningfully lift platform GMV [HYPOTHETICAL]. [→ §commerce]
- **MONITOR eCat ONLINE GROWTH**: eCat Online order share has grown to 47% LTM and 55% in April 2026 MTD. If this trend continues, optimizing the online buyer experience could accelerate self-service revenue without additional rep effort [HYPOTHETICAL]. [→ §commerce]
